battle.name: 黑鷹戰爭
battle.theater: 伊利諾伊州北部與威斯康星西南部
battle.brief: 一八三二年四月至八月，黑鷹率約五百名戰士與六百名老幼再渡密西西比河，回到伊利諾伊州取地；八月二日，其部眾在威斯康星州巴德艾克斯河畔被美軍截斷。雙方手中的滑膛火槍，正是十六世紀西班牙火繩槍銃一路傳下來的後裔。

kit.name: 火繩槍銃
kit.history: 比步槍輕的長槍。西班牙人帶著它上船，也帶著它進了美洲。

countries: 交戰一方是美利堅合眾國：西部軍區的常備軍由布里格adier將軍亨利·阿特金森率領，駐守密西西比河上游的亞姆斯特朗堡、克勞福德堡、溫尼巴哥堡等據點，其後由溫菲爾德·斯科特中將接掌戰區指揮。州與地方民兵是美方的另一根支柱，伊利諾伊州州長約翰·雷諾茲一八三二年四月下旬在比爾茲敦召集義民兵，志願者達 2,100 人，分編五個團，後重組為阿特金森所稱的「邊疆軍團」，騎兵多由密歇根、威斯康星與伊利諾伊各郡的臨時志願騎手充任；伊利諾伊一州先後參戰民兵估計有六至七千人。聯邦政府也藉印第安事務官約瑟夫·M·斯特里特在草原角招募原住民盟軍，計有瓦巴沙與勒阿克率領的達科他戰士約八十人、梅諾米尼四十餘人，以及數支霍-Chunk 部落，名義上歸伊利諾伊民兵上校威廉·S·漢彌爾頓節制。另一方是蘇克與梅斯基基（福克斯）兩族的武裝集團，史稱「英國幫」，由戰首黑鷹率領，旗下約五十名蘇克人、六十至七十名基卡普人擔任作戰主力，另有霍-Chunk 與波塔瓦托米戰士參與；兩族聯合總人口約六千人，英國幫本身則是一支約一千一百人的隊伍，其中約五百人為可出戰的戰士。
countriesEn: The American side was the United States: regulars of the Western Department under Brigadier General Henry Atkinson, holding posts along the upper Mississippi such as Fort Armstrong on Rock Island, Fort Crawford and Fort Winnebago, and later the field command of Major General Winfield Scott. State and local militias were the second pillar. Illinois governor John Reynolds called out volunteers, and by late April 1832 some 2,100 Illinois militiamen had assembled; they were reorganized into Atkinson's "Army of the Frontier", whose mounted ranks came from volunteer horsemen in the counties of Illinois, Michigan and Wisconsin Territory. Federal Indian agents also recruited Native allies: agent Joseph M. Street assembled about 225 warriors at Prairie du Chien, roughly eighty Dakotas under Wabasha and L'Arc, forty Menominee, and several Ho-Chunk bands, nominally under militia colonel William S. Hamilton. On the other side stood the armed following of the Sauk and Meskwaki (Fox), known as the "British Band", led by the war captain Black Hawk; around fifty Sauks and sixty to seventy Kickapoos made up the fighting core, joined by Ho-Chunk and Potawatomi warriors. The two tribes together numbered about 6,000 people, while the British Band itself was a column of roughly 1,100, of whom about 500 were warriors.
people: 黑鷹是蘇克人中的戰首，年已六十有餘，一八一二戰爭時曾與美國交戰；他並非世襲的文職首領，卻自一八二九年起成為反對遷徙一派的領袖，其兄尼波普身為文職首領，自加拿大馬爾登堡歸來後帶回「英軍將援助我方」的說法，史家後來批評為一廂情願。瓦博克希克（白人稱「溫尼巴戈先知」）為薩滿出身、族內最高文職首領，其先知村聚居約二百人，他曾勸黑鷹勿以武力相向，戰後卻與黑鷹一同被俘。美國一方，以阿特金森最關鍵：他於四月十二日抵達羅克島的亞姆斯特朗堡，四月十三日致函雷諾茲求援並誇大威脅，促成民兵入局；六月十五日安德魯·傑克遜總統改派斯科特接任，斯科特集結約九百五十人，卻因霍亂病倒與逃亡減至約三百五十人，趕到前線時已無戰可打。密歇根民兵上校亨利·多奇是最精於追擊的指揮官，他於六月十六日僅以二十九名騎手在佩卡托尼卡河一役得手，七月十五日又與詹姆斯·D·亨利自溫尼巴哥堡出發追擊。扎卡里·泰勒中尉在八月二日巴德艾克斯之役後接管俘虜，傑斐遜·戴維斯與羅伯特·安德森押解囚犯赴傑斐遜兵營；二十三歲的亞伯拉罕·林肯先出任民兵連長，後自願降為列兵，隨軍服務但未接戰。
peopleEn: Black Hawk was a Sauk war captain past sixty, a veteran of the War of 1812; he held no hereditary civil office, yet from 1829 he led the faction that refused removal, while his brother Neapope, a civil chief, brought back from Fort Malden in Canada the news that the British would support them, a claim later dismissed by historians as wishful thinking. Wabokieshiek (White Cloud), a shaman and the highest civil chief of the band, whose village of Prophetstown held about 200 people, counselled against armed conflict yet surrendered alongside Black Hawk. On the American side Atkinson stands first: he reached Fort Armstrong on April 12 and wrote to Reynolds on April 13 seeking militia support and pressing the point of imminent war. On June 15 President Andrew Jackson replaced him with Winfield Scott, who gathered about 950 troops but was reduced by cholera to roughly 350 effective men and arrived too late to fight. Michigan colonel Henry Dodge proved the finest pursuer, winning at Pecatonica on June 16 with only 29 mounted men and setting out from Fort Winnebago on July 15 with James D. Henry. Zachary Taylor took custody of the prisoners after Bad Axe, and Jefferson Davis and Robert Anderson escorted them to Jefferson Barracks; twenty-three-year-old Abraham Lincoln first served as a militia company captain and then re-enlisted as a private, serving without seeing combat.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是十六世紀中葉的西班牙火繩槍銃（arquebus）：比主力步槍更輕的長槍，火繩點火，槍口裝鉛彈；西班牙人帶著它上船，也帶著它進了美洲，是十六世紀海外作戰最通用的輕型火器。要看它在黑鷹戰爭中的位置，須沿血脈往後追：火繩機件改為燧發、長管滑膛化之後，到一八三二年它已化身為英國幫手中的燧發商槍（trade musket）與燧發手槍，也正是美軍步兵一八一六年式、一八一九式滑膛燧發步槍的同一條技術源流，差別只在機件與槍重的演進。英國幫的火力核心就是這些沿英國、底特律與聖路易斯商路流入口岸的商槍與手槍，輔以弓、矛、斧頭與獸皮；黑鷹隊中還帶著一名歐裔鐵匠，專職修整與照顧自家火槍，在黑火藥時代這是極大的優勢。相對地，美軍裝備整齊：民兵多持滑膛民兵步槍與維吉尼亞式燧發獵槍，常備軍使用口徑約 0.54 英寸、彈重約八磅的一八一六年式步槍；更關鍵的是彈藥，常備軍與志願騎兵靠密西西比河上的汽船輸送火藥與鉛彈，英國幫的商槍彈藥只能靠襲奪與零星交易補充，到七、八月已近乎耗盡。八月初在巴德艾克斯河口攔截他們的汽船「戰士號」上還架著一門小型火炮，以霰彈壓制正在涉渡的隊伍。從十六世紀火繩槍銃延伸出的這條火藥武器線，最後就這樣收束了整場戰爭。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the sixteenth-century Spanish arquebus: a long gun lighter than a heavy musket, fired by a matchlock, ball and powder loaded at the muzzle; Spaniards carried it to sea and into the Americas as the commonest light arm of overseas campaigning. To place it in the Black Hawk War one must follow the line of descent: the matchlock gave way to the flintlock and the long barrel was standardized as a smoothbore, and by 1832 the arquebus had become the flintlock trade musket and flintlock pistol carried by Sauk and Meskwaki fighters, and equally the technical ancestor of the Model 1816 and Model 1819 smoothbore flintlock muskets carried by American infantry, the difference lying only in the evolution of mechanism and weight. The firepower of the British Band was precisely this: trade muskets and pistols obtained along the British, Detroit and St. Louis trading routes, used alongside bows, lances, tomahawks and hides; the band also had a European blacksmith among them who kept the guns in repair, a decisive advantage in the age of black powder. The Americans were more evenly supplied: militia carried smoothbore militia muskets and Virginia-style flintlock hunting rifles, regulars the Model 1816 musket of about 0.54 inch calibre firing an eight-pound ball; above all ammunition flowed by steamboat up the Mississippi, while the British Band's powder and ball had to be taken in raids or bought piecemeal, and by July and August were nearly exhausted. The steamboat Warrior, which intercepted the band at the mouth of the Bad Axe in August, carried a small cannon that fired canister over the heads of men in the water; that line of black-powder ordnance, the direct heir of the arquebus, closed the war.
tactics: 英國幫的戰法建立在「家眷同行」的結構上：老幼婦孺與非戰鬥者隨大隊遷移，戰士護其兩翼，遇敵即散入密林、沼澤與河岸樹蔭，以零散射擊消耗追兵。他們最著名的一手是白旗議和：一八三二年五月十四日黃昏，黑鷹派人持白旗接近斯蒂爾曼民兵營，遭扣押並被開火殺害，此後白旗在美軍眼中變成「誘敵伏擊」的代名詞，所有往後交涉都為之硬化。當晚四十名戰士夜襲民兵營，是英國幫唯一一次主動攻擊建制民兵，得手全靠密林地形、美軍對夜襲的陌生，以及民兵營地哨戒鬆散。真正的主軸是美軍的騎兵追擊：多奇、詹姆斯·D·亨利等以小隊分散搜索，靠馬匹速度切斷退路，七月下旬在威斯康星高地迫使黑鷹以五十名蘇克人及六十至七十名基卡普人擔任後衛，掩護大隊渡過威斯康星河，這是黑鷹全軍最出色的軍事動作。最後一役的關鍵是汽船：「戰士號」沿河巡弋，船上小炮封鎖渡口，岸上常備軍與民兵以整齊的齊射壓制正在涉水的人，梅諾米尼與達科他盟軍則在下游追截殘部。整體而言，美軍全程沒有騎兵，行軍縱隊與汽船後勤拖慢了初期的推進；而英國幫既無後方補給，又須照顧大批非戰鬥者，戰術主動權隨彈藥耗盡而喪失。
tacticsEn: The British Band fought as a moving household: non-combatants, women and children travelled with the column while warriors covered its flanks, then dispersed into woodland, marsh and riverbank cover to break up pursuit. Their most famous device was the white flag. On the evening of May 14 Black Hawk sent men under a flag of truce toward Stillman's camp; they were detained and shot, and from that day the white flag was read in American ranks as the cover for an ambush, which hardened every later parley. That night attack, fought by forty warriors against a militia camp, was the only deliberate offensive the British Band ever launched against formed militia, and it succeeded precisely because the woods were the Americans' weak ground, the camp's picket was thin and the militia had no confidence in the dark. American mounted pursuit was the spine of the campaign: Dodge and James D. Henry rode out in scattered detachments, used the speed of their horses to cut the road of retreat, and at Wisconsin Heights in late July forced Black Hawk to cover the crossing of the Wisconsin River with about fifty Sauks and sixty to seventy Kickapoos, the finest piece of generalship he showed. The final action turned on a steamboat: the Warrior patrolled the river, its small cannon sealing the crossing, while regulars and militia on the bank delivered disciplined volleys into men already in the water, and Menominee and Dakota allies cut off the remnant downstream. Overall, the absence of cavalry, the dependence of the American column on its wagon train and steamboat supply line, and the absence of any resupply behind the British Band explain American slowness in April and the American victory in August.
data: 這場戰爭可核的數字不少。英國幫約一千一百人，其中約五百人為戰士、六百人為老幼婦孺；蘇克與福克斯兩族當時總人口約六千人，其中約八百人選擇抗拒遷徙，另有二百餘名基卡普人與若干波塔瓦托米、霍-Chunk 加入。背景的《聖路易條約》以約 2,200 美元貨品加每年 1,000 美元貨品取得密西西比河以東大片土地，價額與界線雙方理解不一。一八三二年四月二十二日集結於比爾茲敦的伊利諾伊民兵志願者達 2,100 人，編為五個團；六月重編的「邊疆軍團」有 629 名常備步兵與 3,196 名騎兵民兵，其中可作戰者約 450 名常備兵與 2,100 名民兵；伊利諾伊一州先後參戰民兵估計六至七千人，多奇上校的騎兵營最多時約 250 人，而六月十六日佩卡托尼卡一役只投入 29 名騎手。作戰方一方的官方陣亡統計為 77 人（不含斯科特縱隊因霍亂死亡者）；英國幫方面一般估算死亡 450 至 600 人，約為渡河時總數的一半，其中七月下旬威斯康星高地一役民兵僅陣亡 1 人而斃傷多達 68 名戰士，八月二日巴德艾克斯一役美方陣亡 14 人、英國幫陣亡至少 260 人，其中約 110 人溺斃；五月十四日斯台爾曼河一役，四十名戰士擊殺 12 名民兵而己方陣亡 3 人。裝備與行政數字同樣可查：斯科特集合約 950 名士兵，因霍亂減至約 350 人；阿特金森四月八日自傑斐遜兵營出發時僅約 220 名士兵；美方懸賞捕拿黑鷹的價碼是 100 美元加 40 匹馬。戰後的價碼更以土地計：蘇克與福克斯售出約 600 萬英畝土地，年金 2 萬美元、期三十年；霍-Chunk 則以威斯康星河以南全部土地換取愛荷華一條四十英里寬的地帶與每年 1 萬美元、為期二十七年。
dataEn: The figures for this war are unusually well documented. The British Band counted about 1,100 people, roughly 500 of them warriors, with 600 women, children and elders; the Sauk and Meskwaki together numbered about 6,000, of whom some 800 chose to resist removal, joined by more than 200 Kickapoos and a handful of Potawatomi and Ho-Chunk. The background treaty of St. Louis, 1804, "bought" a vast area east of the Mississippi for about $2,200 in goods plus $1,000 a year in goods, a price and a boundary the two sides understood differently. On April 22, 1832 some 2,100 Illinois militia volunteers assembled at Beardstown in five regiments; the "Army of the Frontier" formed in June contained 629 regular infantry and 3,196 mounted militia, of whom about 450 regulars and 2,100 militiamen were available for campaigning; Illinois alone put six to seven thousand men into the field, and Dodge's mounted battalion numbered about 250 at its strongest, though only 29 horsemen rode into the action at Pecatonica on June 16. American military dead are officially counted at 77, excluding the cholera dead of Scott's column; Native losses are estimated at 450 to 600, about half of those who had crossed the river. At Wisconsin Heights in late July the militia lost one man while killing as many as 68 warriors; at Bad Axe on August 2 the Americans lost 14 and the British Band at least 260, of whom about 110 drowned; on May 14 forty warriors at Stillman's Run killed 12 militiamen and lost three of their own. On the materiel and administrative side Scott collected about 950 men and fell to roughly 350 through cholera, Atkinson left Jefferson Barracks on April 8 with only about 220 soldiers, and the reward for Black Hawk's capture was set at $100 and forty horses. The final price was paid in land: the Sauks and Meskwakis sold about 6 million acres for $20,000 a year for thirty years, while the Ho-Chunk ceded everything south of the Wisconsin River in exchange for a forty-mile strip in Iowa and $10,000 a year for twenty-seven years.
cause: 導火線是一紙雙方理解不同的條約。一八零四年，密蘇里地區總督威廉·亨利·哈里森在聖路易斯與一批蘇克、福克斯首領議定條約，以約 2,200 美元貨品加每年 1,000 美元貨品取得密西西比河以東大片土地，支付額相對土地價值極為菲薄，且首領未曾獲得部族議會授權。協議容許該兩族繼續居住，直至美國將土地售予拓殖者；一八二八年政府開始實測出售，黑鷹拒絕承認，白雲一派則接受並西遷。一八二九年主村索克努克（Saukenuk）被拓殖者佔據，黑鷹一派返抵後又被迫遷走，直到一八三零年才再次回到石河畔。此後簽訂一八三一年六月三十日與蓋恩斯將軍的協議，承諾不再東渡；然而一八三零至三一年洪水與歉收造成飢荒，黑鷹的追隨者飢寒交迫，又聽信尼波普自加拿大帶回的「英軍會援助」消息，遂於一八三二年四月五日攜約一千一百人東渡。直接引爆點是五月十四日斯台爾曼河之夜戰：黑鷹認為持白旗者被美軍扣押殺害，憤而夜襲；白宮與陸軍部長劉易斯·卡斯隨即拒絕任何外交解決，執意要一場「大勝」作為對其他部族的示例。
causeEn: The trigger was a treaty nobody had read the same way. In 1804 Missouri territorial governor William Henry Harrison negotiated at St. Louis with a group of Sauk and Fox leaders, obtaining a vast area east of the Mississippi for about $2,200 in goods plus $1,000 a year in goods — a small price for the land, and the chiefs had not been authorized by their councils. The agreement allowed the tribes to keep living there until the United States sold the land to settlers; surveying for sale began in 1828, Black Hawk refused to concede, and the faction of White Cloud accepted and moved west. In 1829 squatters occupied the village of Saukenuk, and Black Hawk's people were driven off, returning to the Rock River only in 1830. An agreement of June 30, 1831 with General Gaines bound the band not to cross the Mississippi again; then the floods and crop failures of 1830 and 1831 brought famine, Neapope returned from Canada with news of British support, and on April 5, 1832 some 1,100 people crossed eastward. The immediate spark was the night of May 14 at Stillman's Run: Black Hawk held that his emissaries under a white flag had been detained and shot, and struck back that night. From then on the White House and Secretary of War Lewis Cass refused any negotiated settlement, wanting a crushing victory as an example to other tribes.
impact: 這場戰爭終結了舊西北地區原住民的武裝抵抗，也把「印地安人遷徙」從政策變成既成事實。戰後聯邦官員以條約收購蘇克與福克斯在愛荷華約 600 萬英畝土地，並在霍-Chunk 條約中取得威斯康星河以南全部土地；黑鷹部眾被安置於「中立地帶」邊緣，一八三七至三八年，阿特金森以軍隊強制遷走最後一批蘇克與福克斯人，愛荷華的祖地就此告一段落。軍制上的教訓更為直接：美軍此役全程沒有騎兵，追擊全靠臨時志願騎手，國會因此在戰後設立由亨利·多奇指揮的騎兵探營中隊，並於一八三三年擴編為第一騎兵團，成為此後追蹤平原部族的常設骨幹。政治上，這是一場「小兵將領」的戰爭：參與者中有七位後來當上美國參議員、四位伊利諾伊州州長，以及密歇根、內布拉斯加與威斯康星領地的未來州長，最受矚目的是二十三歲的亞伯拉罕·林肯，他在戰中未發一槍，卻在退伍後以伊利諾伊州眾議員身分，把黑鷹戰爭的土地交易與政府對待俘虜的處置推上國會辯論。另一面，黑鷹被解往華盛頓、紐約等地「示眾」參觀，成為「高貴的野蠻人」神話的活教材；他回到愛荷華後最終在德莫因河畔安置下來，一八三八年去世，一八三九年遺骨由後人迎回伊利諾伊安葬。
impactEn: The war ended armed Native resistance in the Old Northwest and turned removal from policy into accomplished fact. Federal officials bought out the Sauk and Meskwaki claims to about 6 million acres in eastern Iowa and took the Ho-Chunk land south of the Wisconsin River; the survivors were pushed to the edge of the "Neutral Ground", and in 1837-38 Atkinson used troops to complete the removal of the last Sauks and Foxes to Kansas. The military lesson was blunt: the United States had no cavalry throughout the campaign and relied on temporary mounted volunteers, so Congress created the Mounted Ranger Battalion under Henry Dodge and expanded it into the 1st Cavalry Regiment in 1833, the core of the later Plains campaigns. Politically it was a war of junior officers — seven future United States senators, four future governors of Illinois, future governors of Michigan, Nebraska and Wisconsin Territory, and, most famous, the twenty-three-year-old Abraham Lincoln, who fired no shot in the campaign but as an Illinois congressman later carried the Black Hawk lands and the government's treatment of the prisoners into congressional debate. Black Hawk himself was taken to Washington and New York on display, becoming a living illustration of the "noble savage"; he was finally settled on the Des Moines River in Iowa, died there in 1838, and in 1839 his remains were brought back to Illinois by his family.
result: 以軍事結果論，這是一場徹底的美方勝利。英國幫到七月已減至不足六百人，八月初僅餘約五百人，其中約一百五十人為戰士；七月下旬黑鷹在威斯康星高地以五十名蘇克人與六十至七十名基卡普人掩護大隊渡過威斯康星河，隨即被七百五十名民兵擊潰；八月一日汽船「戰士號」在巴德艾克斯河口以小炮與槍火攔截，八月二日晨美軍追及殘部，展開全戰最後一役。戰後瓦巴沙率領的達科他人在雪松河一役再殲 68 人、俘 22 人；梅諾米尼一個近三百人的營雖遲到一步，仍在後續追捕中擊殺數名戰士。八月二十七日，黑鷹與瓦博克希克終於在草原角向印第安事務官約瑟夫·斯特里特投降，扎卡里·泰勒接管囚人；戰事結束時黑鷹與另外十九名首領一度關押於傑斐遜兵營，一八三三年四月黑鷹、瓦博克希克、尼波普等五人被轉往維吉尼亞門羅堡，隨後在華盛頓與安德魯·傑克遜總統短暫會面，再自六月四日起被安排遊覽巴爾的摩、費城與紐約。戰爭最終沒有為蘇克人換來任何土地：英國幫被拆散，多數人留在愛荷華並被逐步推向西方，另有少數人北上投奔奧吉布瓦人；黑鷹本人則在囚禁與東行巡遊之後回到愛荷華，一八三八年在德莫因河畔度過餘生。這場戰爭真正的產物，是美方「必勝」的敘事與一紙紙土地條約。
resultEn: Militarily this was a complete American victory. The British Band was reduced to fewer than 600 people by July and about 500 by early August, of whom some 150 were warriors. At Wisconsin Heights in late July Black Hawk covered the crossing of the Wisconsin River with about fifty Sauks and sixty to seventy Kickapoos and was then broken by 750 militiamen; on August 1 the steamboat Warrior with its small cannon intercepted the band at the mouth of the Bad Axe, and on the morning of August 2 the Americans overtook the remnant and fought the last action of the war. Afterwards the Dakotas under Wabasha struck the fugitives along the Cedar River, killing 68 and taking 22 prisoners, and a Menominee battalion, arriving a day too late, killed several warriors in the pursuit that followed. With the $100 and forty horses reward circulating, Black Hawk and Wabokieshiek surrendered at Prairie du Chien to agent Joseph Street on August 27; Zachary Taylor took custody, and nineteen leaders were held at Jefferson Barracks, five of them — Black Hawk, Wabokieshiek, Neapope and two others — transferred to Fort Monroe, Virginia, in April 1833, where they met President Jackson briefly in Washington before being taken on a tour of Baltimore, Philadelphia and New York from June 4. The war bought no land for the Sauk: the British Band was broken up, most of its people stayed in Iowa to be pushed west in stages, a few went north to the Ojibwe, and Black Hawk himself, after a year of captivity and a tour of the eastern cities, ended his days on the Des Moines River in 1838. The real product of the war was an American narrative of inevitable victory and a series of land treaties.
